points.text: The answer says that a crossing line carries no money figure — cross and refund record the day, the class and the note only — so every counting of past takings prices old lines through whatever fare table stands at the moment of counting.
The answer says that set_fare replaces the one undated figure a class has, so once a fare changes the figure that was in force on any earlier day is gone from the book.
The answer says that a refund is priced off the fare table as it stands when the refund is given, so after a fare change the box hands back a different sum than it took for that same crossing.

The answer tells apart the fare table's two uses in this code: pricing a crossing not yet made, where the figure as it stands is the right one, and restating money already taken, where it is not the same question.
The answer commits to exactly one ruling — a defect to be put right, or the book's intended way of keeping accounts — and argues for it against the other reading.

disqualifiers.text: The answer claims that the sums actually taken at the box for past crossings can be recovered from the book as it stands.
